observation: Rebuilding this emblem from shapes and typed text stalled around 40/100 in the early tries, while tracing the redraw with lifted text reached 97.6/100 with every word still live and audited. Two rough edges: poster_fit copies the reference's flaws (the reference's English ran past the end of its bar), and setting the English cleanly inside its bars took a script outside funkbox (find the straight run of the bar, size the text down until it fits with a margin, centre it); the first fit used a regular italic that came out small, a condensed italic filled the bars about 40% better.
suggestion: Give text layers a 'fit_inside' option: a region of the artwork (a colour plus a point, or a traced shape) the words must stay inside with a margin, sized to the largest that fits and centred along it, with condensed faces tried when one is allowed; poster_fit could then respect it instead of chasing a flawed reference.
would_enable: A one-call recreate of any badge or logo with its words as live text, in about a minute instead of two.

observation: Creator guides for local AI video this season put the entry ticket at a 24 GB card for lighter or offloaded setups and 48 GB+ for 14B-class models, so many creators assume local video is out of reach without a big GPU. funkbox already renders without one, but on a fresh headless Linux box (today's cloud run) it first failed with 'could not create an OpenGL 3.3 context; egl: libEGL.so not loaded' and only worked after installing libegl1, libegl-mesa0 and libgl1-mesa-dri by hand; nothing in the error said which packages to install.
suggestion: Add `python -m funkbox doctor`: probe the GL backends (native, EGL, software llvmpipe), and when EGL is missing print the exact install command for the detected distro (apt/dnf/pacman) and set FUNK_GL_BACKEND automatically when only software GL works. Have render and the MCP server show the same hint instead of the bare GLUnavailable error, and report the backend in M-machine-style one-liners.
would_enable: A how-to promo: 'from a bare cloud VM to a rendered Short in 3 commands, no GPU' with the doctor output on a code card and a measured end-to-end time.

observation: The animated-machine genre (Claude building working engines, escapements and differentials as code; CellCog 2026-10-12, Stork.AI 2026-10-23) lives or dies on the mechanism being right: teeth that actually mesh and parts that move in step. Making today's gear train in funkbox meant hand-deriving pitch radii, centre distances and each gear's mesh phase so the teeth interleave, and picking tooth counts so every gear makes a whole number of turns per loop; nothing in funkbox helps with either, and a wrong phase only shows up when you look at frames.
suggestion: Add a small mechanism library to the shader prelude: gear(p, centre, teeth, angle) as an SDF with a shared module, meshWith(gearA, direction, teeth) that returns the meshed gear's centre and phase, and crank/slider helpers. Have loop_write_shader report each gear's turns per loop and warn when one is not a whole number (the loop would jump). Ship one example (examples/gear_train.frag) and a 'machine' preset.
would_enable: A how-to promo: 'a clock escapement or a 4-gear train in 10 lines of GLSL', with the loop check naming the turns per loop on a code card, and a series of mechanism loops (escapement, Geneva drive, planetary gears).

observation: Ad-format guidance this season asks for the same ad in several shapes: Google Ads recommends uploading 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1 versions, and vendor guides map 4:5/1:1 to feeds and 9:16 to Reels. funkbox already renders every shape from one reel, but making today's promo showed the gap after rendering: to show or ship the set I had to run `reel render --format` once per shape (three runs, about 45-70 s each on a 4-core CPU), then hand-build a contact sheet with ffmpeg to check each shape's captions, and nothing tells you which format a caption box crowds once the frame changes shape.
suggestion: Add `reel render --all-formats --sheet`: render every declared format in one call and write formats.png, a side-by-side sheet of each format at the same 3-4 timestamps, plus a per-format line in the text audit (strings checked, exact) so one audit covers the whole set. Have `validate` report, per format, any caption whose box covers more than a set share of the subject or another caption.
would_enable: A behind-the-scenes promo with measured numbers for the whole set: 'four shapes of one ad, rendered in N seconds, every caption audited in every shape', with the formats sheet as the hero shot.

observation: Ad-testing guides this year keep telling creators to ship many variants of one ad, each with a different first scene or hook, and to change one variable per batch (influee's 'Doubling ROAS by Creating Variations of the Same Ad', videotok's creative-testing workflow, segwise on AI UGC testing). In funkbox today each variant means hand-copying the reel.json and copy.json and rendering them one by one.
suggestion: Add `funkbox reel variants <reel> --swap shots[0]=a.json,b.json,c.json` (and an MCP tool reel_variants): one shot list, N alternatives for a named shot or copy id, rendered as N files named by variant, each with its own text audit, plus a contact sheet (the new grid shot can build it) of the first second of every variant so a person can pick before uploading.
would_enable: A how-to promo: 'Five hooks, one shot list': five openings of the demo ad rendered in one command and shown as a grid, each text-audited.

observation: Creators keep losing generations to garbled on-screen text in AI video: Adobe Community threads describe clips that misspell a name or word ('doesn't' three times, 'Housston') and hundreds to ~2,000 credits spent regenerating; guides (CoreReflex, gptproto) say the fix is to keep text out of the generation and add it in an editor afterward. funkbox already adds exact, audited captions on top, but it cannot remove the wrong text a model already baked into a clip.
suggestion: Bring image_trace's lift_text idea to video: a reel source option such as {"video": "clip.mp4", "cover_text": {"rect": [x,y,w,h], "copy_id": "sign"}} that tracks a rectangle across the clip (or takes keyed rects), covers the baked-in text with a blurred or colour-matched patch, and sets the approved line in its place as live text that follows the rect, so the text audit covers it like any caption.
would_enable: A before/after promo: a generated clip with a misspelled sign, fixed in one shot-list line, with the audit proving the new sign exact.

observation: Word-by-word 'karaoke' captions with the current word highlighted are described across 2026 short-form caption guides as the default Shorts/Reels/TikTok style, and the tools that make them time each word from Whisper word timestamps (spoken audio). funkbox's new pill is timed from a characters-per-second estimate (docs/reel.md: 'The voice path has no per-word timings yet, so on voiced shots the pill can drift from the spoken word'), and a style cannot pick WHICH words to emphasise; guides and builders recommend highlighting only key words (about 15-20%), e.g. numbers and punchlines.
suggestion: Two steps for the word highlight: (1) take per-word timings from the local voiceover (Piper can emit phoneme durations; or a local forced-alignment pass) so the pill lands on the spoken word on voiced shots; (2) let the copy deck mark emphasis words (e.g. a 'stress' list per copy line, or *word* markup that the audit strips) so the pill or a colour change hits only those, with the text audit still checking the plain text.
would_enable: A voiced explainer Short where the pill lands on each spoken word and only the key numbers light up, with the audit still proving the words are the approved copy.
